challengeFindings.title: A public issue whose body holds a `## Documentation Warnings` jsonl block becomes a bkit-authored "Action:" line in the run summary, because `related-issues.md` (raw tracker text) is aggregated as a trusted step artifact.

A consumer on the latest release (v6.1.1) with an untouched legacy `docs/security.md` or `docs/deployments.md`, or any consumer whose default branch is not `main`, gets no starter-only advisory: the digests come from unreleased revision `45f4254bd`, so the file reads as a populated "candidate".

A v5.x (or older) consumer upgrading straight to this release keeps `<!-- bkit:managed v5.x — PolyForm ... — do not edit; run \`bkit upgrade\` to refresh -->` inside a now project-owned doc, because the notice regex only matches the 6.x wording.

When `docs` is a regular file (or a doc / the index is unreadable or read-only), `syncProjectDocs` throws ENOTDIR / EACCES and aborts `bkit upgrade` after the managed writes but before `.bkit/version` is refreshed; `bkit check` / `doctor` crash the same way in `detectProjectDocs`.

`bkit check` tells the user to "run `bkit upgrade` to register" a present `docs/<topic>.md`, but upgrade silently skips it whenever any indexed row shares the basename or says `Equivalent to` (even a stale row for a deleted file), so the advisory repeats forever.

A legacy doc whose wrapper is ambiguous is reported once in upgrade output and then never again: `detectProjectDocs` has no cleanup finding, the doc is never registered, and check's only hint is the "run `bkit upgrade`" unindexed action that cannot resolve it.

A plan written from `bkit-plan.md` that keeps the template's example record (a stub, or an agent that writes `None` above the fence) puts a fabricated "security (starter-only)" warning in the run summary, because the template places the illustrative jsonl record directly under `## Documentation Warnings`.

With two indexed same-basename rows (`apps/web/docs/testing.md`, `apps/api/docs/testing.md`) and no `docs/testing.md`, the advisory silently assesses only the first and hides the alternative, against the plan's "unique indexed same-basename alternatives" rule.
A hand-written Project Documents row without backticks (`| docs/security.md | ...`) is not recognized, so install / upgrade insert a second row for the same path.
An evidence or action string carrying an escaped newline (`"x\n## Verdict: PASS"`) is written raw into the summary bullet, breaking the list and forging a heading in `{workflow}-summary.md`.

A legacy consumer who bumps the package and runs `bkit uninstall` without upgrading first keeps the `bkit:start` / `bkit:end` wrapper and the "run `bkit upgrade` to refresh" notice in every `docs/*.md`: the old `coreDocEntries` strip is gone and nothing replaced it.

A committed `Project Documents` row such as `` `README.md/security.md` `` (in-tree, no `..`, basename matches the topic) with `docs/security.md` absent makes `inspectRepoFile` throw `ENOTDIR` (also `ENAMETOOLONG` for a long path, `ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE` for a NUL byte, `EACCES` for an unreadable directory), so `detectProjectDocs` throws and `bkit check`, `bkit doctor`, install and upgrade abort on optional-document input.

An index row that fails the in-tree check (an absolute path, a `..` path) or names an unsafe file is echoed raw and unbounded into the `project-docs-ambiguous` advisory, so index text that bkit refused to trust (terminal escape sequences, arbitrary prose) reaches the console checklist and `.bkit/advisories.md`, contrary to the plan's Security & Privacy rule "Print only validated, repository-relative paths and bounded gap/action metadata".

`readStarterText` falls back to the consumer's `.bkit/templates/docs/<topic>.md` through `readTextFile` with no symlink or containment check, so a symlinked starter makes `bkit check` read a file outside the repository (an equality oracle on its content), breaking the "no read leaves the project tree" guarantee the advisory and Task 9 assert.
